newsitem.title: POLAND: FORECAST - Poland to lure $30 bln FDI by 2000 - agency.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Poland to lure $30 bln FDI by 2000 - agency.

text.p: Poland is likely to attract about $30 billion in foreign direct investment (FDI) in the 10 years to 2000, the government's Foreign Investment Agency (PAIZ) said on Wednesday.
"It is realistic to assume that the investment will reach $30 billion until 2000," PAIZ deputy president Adam Laskowski told a news conference.
In July, foreign direct investment in Poland had exceeded $10 billion since the 1990 launch of market reforms.
Laskowski said investors from Far East countries were likely to start flocking to Poland in the next few years, after a period dominated by companies from the United States and the European Union.
Laskowski said the investment might reach between $4.5 billion and $5 billion in 1996 alone. PAIZ earlier forecast the investment inflow to be $4 billion this year.
